To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we define a notion of activity which generalizes the two notions of Tutte and Bernardi.

the $\Delta$ activity can be defined for all planar graphs, it has a nice interpretation, it is related to the Tutte polynomial, it can be used to define the Tutte polynomial for non planar graphs, and it is related to other known activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Tutte polynomials of matroids, and more precisely with their expression in terms of activities.
the following question: how can we understand the Tutte polynomial as a function of its variables?
the following question: what is the most natural definition of the activity?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the $\Delta$ activities are the only activities that give a correct description of the Tutte polynomials.
the $\Delta$ activity is the most natural notion of activity for graphs, and that the other activities are just particular cases of the $\Delta$ one.
Tutte's polynomial of a graph is a polynomial in two variables $x,y$ which depends on a choice of a $\Delta$-active function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all the Tutte polynomials of a graph $G$ are equal, and that the coefficients of the Tutte polynomial are the number of $G$-colorings of the graphs of a given $\Delta$-degree.
the Tutte polynomial can be seen as a polynomial in two activities.
the Tutte polynomial is a function of a graph, an ordering of the vertices, and a function $\Delta$ on the edges, and that the different expressions are just different ways of choosing $\Delta$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Tutte polynomial can be expressed as a sum of $\Delta$-activities.
the Tutte polynomial is not only a function of the number of connected components of the graph, but also a function of the activity.
the notion of activity is not a unique one, but that it can be generalized to other settings.
